title: Familiar words within a changing mood

captions.physics: Using a shared language of promises
captions.energy: Honouring the recognised meaning of words
captions.emotions: Feeling your response to words change

meaning: A shared language of promises gives you understandable support even when a familiar phrase brings a different feeling at different times.
text: The same phrase can sound different to you on different days. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha gives speech recognisable forms: shared promises, accepted rules and words of respect. The Hierophant in energy concerns another layer, the wish to honour a meaning both people recognise. The Wheel of Fortune in emotions makes the response changeable. A familiar promise can comfort today and feel too general tomorrow. Your shared language keeps its value while leaving the living experience of its speakers present.

For example, “I’m always on your side” feels warm after one disagreement, while after another it prompts a question about what that means now. **A promise’s meaning lives beside a changing feeling.** You can say whether listening, help with a reply or room for an awkward first sentence is needed. Familiar words then open discussion of actual participation, leaving each person free from performing the same relief whenever reassurance is repeated.

The difficulty appears if a changed response seems to mean the promise has lost all value. A more solemn repetition or the earlier reaction seems necessary. Preserving shared meaning stays a kind intention. Asking about the present request allows support to change its concrete form without making every mood require fresh proof that your words were serious.
